name: EIA/TIA-232 family and the PC serial-port implementation

era.notes: This reading slice compares V.24 (02/2000), IBM PC/5150 April 1984, TI September 2002, and the IBM AT Serial/Parallel Adapter chapter dated August 31, 1984 in Options and Adapters Volume 2 (volume edition: April 1984). These are source dates, not interface lifecycle or first-adoption dates.

physical.notes: IBM AT original documentation distinguishes a 9-contact serial port, a 25-contact parallel port, and the 25-contact end of an optional serial cable; full standard/implementation contact mapping remains gated.

electrical.notes: IBM implementation/UART boundary plus a V.28 (03/1993) significant-level reading exercise, including strict boundaries and fault/polarity exceptions; no complete electrical-standard or device-safety review.

signaling.notes: Data/control and UART framing are distinguished; full timing/framing/version comparison is unfinished.

protocol.notes: Limited to selected DTE/DCE data/control circuit definitions in V.24 (02/2000), not a complete communications protocol.

host.notes: Limited to the IBM PC/5150 April 1984 Technical Reference (publication 6361453) BIOS/8250 services and send/status reading path; no modern OS or USB adapter claims.

ecosystem.notes: IBM PC/5150 external-modem context, a documented IBM AT adapter/optional-cable example, and later TI PC application context only; lifecycle and replacement/continuity research is unfinished.

evidence_summary.notes: Four E1 sources (V.24, IBM publication 6361453, the IBM AT Serial/Parallel Adapter chapter in Options and Adapters Volume 2, and V.28) and one E2 TI application note were used. Each document is counted once, not once per scan, OCR, or page. V.28 was rereviewed from a cached copy on 2026-09-14; hypothetical reading questions are not receiver simulation. No E3 emulation or E4 measurement was performed.

safety_notes: No executable pin-to-pin, null-modem, hot-plug, or TTL-UART-to-RS-232 wiring instructions are provided.
TIA/ISO full-text and edition review, specific endpoint and cable evidence, electrical levels, directions, grounding, power, and hot-plug conditions remain unresolved.
open_questions: Obtain and review the official TIA entry/full text, relevant ISO 2110 editions, and edition differences identified in the source map; the scoped IBM AT 9-contact original-document review is complete.

Resolve the normative scope of IBM's optional-cable all-signals wording versus TI's PC subset wording using the relevant full standards and complete cable documentation; the present functional comparison is not a resolution.
Complete lifecycle, use-case-specific replacement and inheritance research before asserting relationship records.
Establish sources for any selected modern OS, driver, adapter, and reproducible experiment before describing their behavior.
